To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) δ^(13) C and δ^(18) O isotopic values in carbonate strata of the late Famennian Parting Formation and Dyer Formation of western Colorado are highly variable and are not correlated across the Parting– Dyer contact and (b) the isotopic shifts in carbonate strata below the Dyer–Chaffee Formation contact are not correlated across western Colorado, and are likely the result of diagenetic overprinting.
the isotopic signature of the ALFIE event is highly variable across the western U.S. and results from a regional unconformable contact that is linked to a eustatic event.

(1) the Parting– Dyer contact is a regionally extensive unconfor-mity surface that records a relative sea-level fall and associated diagenetic alteration; (2) the unconformity surface is associated with a global eustatic event (Dasberg Event) and a major extinction event (Hangenberg Event); and (3) the isotopic shifts across the unconformity in the Chaffee Group are not global but are a result of local diagenetic alteration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of carbonate diagenesis during relative sea-level fall and the resulting isotopic signatures that can be preserved in the rock record.
understanding the nature and origin of the ALFIE isotopic anomaly, and the role that it may play in global stratigraphy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ALFIE signal, and the isotopic signal associated with the Hangenberg Event, may be a diagenetic signal that results from the alteration of carbonate units in a lowstand setting.

the isotopic shifts associated with ALFIE and Hangenberg events are not global marine signals, but rather the result of diagenetic overprinting of carbonate units during relative sea-level falls associated with these events.
the ALFIE isotopic anomaly is the result of diagenetic overprint associated with a major eustatic event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

diagenesis in carbonate rocks is a major factor that can influence δ^(13) C values, and this is particularly important for rocks that have been exposed to subaerial environments during periods of relative sea-level fall.

the δ^(13C) values in strata below the unconformities are not a global signal of a global event, but are a local signal that is the result of the local conditions at the time of deposition and the local conditions during subsequent lowstand and diagenesis.
δ^(13) C and δ^(18) O values are highly variable across the uppermost Chaffee Group in western Colorado, with the most extreme values associated with unconformities and associated paleokarsts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
δ^(13) C values can vary significantly within a stratigraphic unit, particularly when the unit has undergone significant subaerial exposure and subsequent reburial.
diagenesis can be a powerful control on carbonate isotopic values, and that this diagenetic control can be linked to unconformity surfaces and associated sea-level changes.
the isotopic record of strata below unconformities can be diagenetic in origin and that the degree of diagenetic overprint is highly variable across a basin.
